correctness.rationale: The rate-sum clock has an exact Gamma-times-positive-stable representation by Laplace transforms. The killed nearest-neighbor reflection kernel gives a Gaussian derivative local limit and survival of order inverse square root of operational time. Negative Gamma-stable moments make the survivor-bias transfer uniformly integrable. A direct killed-moment asymptotic plus the heavy-tailed rate moment index alpha proves finite-time q-moment finiteness exactly when q<1+2alpha. The normalized conditional q moments converge by uniform higher-moment bounds. The stopped martingale gives E[X_t;T>t]=h exactly. Numerical verifier passed 110 deterministic tests; they do not substitute for these proofs.

value.rationale: It resolves a natural survivor-observable question left by the first-passage mean: where long-lived walkers lie and which environmental rates they see. The joint clock bias is an explicit structural law. The all-time conditional second-moment transition is physically meaningful and counterintuitive: the same large rate fluctuations that make the mean hit time finite make the nonabsorbed spatial cloud have infinite variance. This is not a pure normalization check or an arbitrary finite slice.
